The systemd examples were tested locally in an **Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS virtual machine running systemd 249**.

2941.title: docs: reduce Secrets Management cheat sheet section 2
2941.body:
## Description

This PR reduces Section 2 ("General Secrets Management") of the Secrets Management Cheat Sheet, as requested in [issue #2793](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/issues/2793).

- **General guidance:** Removed conversational filler and consolidated the guidance on high availability, centralization, least-privilege access, automation, auditing, resilience, policies, and metadata.
- **Automated rotation:** Removed the lengthy Kubernetes YAML example and vendor-specific implementation details. Retained two architectural patterns: dual-credential phased rotation (with cryptographic key retention) and orchestrated multi-step rotation (with safe handling of single-active credential invalidation, idempotency, and testing).
- **Secret delivery:** Clarified the distinction between secret delivery and actual credential rotation at the backing service. Sidecars are described as delivery and refresh mechanisms requiring application reload or restart, with a cross-reference to Section 5.2.
- **Memory protection:** Removed lengthy hardware side-channel discussions while preserving practical memory protection guidance, including memory dumps, swap, secure zeroing, runtime-neutral managed runtime limitations, process separation, and core dump protection.
- **Secret lifecycle:** Consolidated guidance across creation, distribution, rotation, revocation, and expiration. Categorized memorized passwords (per NIST SP 800-63 FAQ #q-b05), TOTP shared secrets, and WebAuthn credentials separately. Removed outdated password delivery recommendations involving SMS and email.
- **Transport security:** Recommended TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 with forward secrecy and strict certificate validation, and framed mutual TLS (mTLS) for zero-trust transport-layer client identity verification.
- **Scope:** Changes are limited to `cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.md`. Section 2 was reduced from approximately 2,728 to 1,836 words (a 32.7% reduction). This PR handles Section 2 separately from the Section 3 changes in PR #2900.

2955.title: Docker Security Cheat Sheet: Swarm note under Rule #5a (#2936, #2951)
2955.body:
Adds a short "Docker Swarm" subsection at the end of Rule #5a, covering both #2936 and #2951 in one PR as requested by the maintainer.

- #2936: Option 1 (binding to `127.0.0.1`) does not apply to Swarm services. A published service port cannot be bound to a host IP ([moby/moby#26696](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/26696)); with the routing mesh it listens on every IP of every node, and `mode=host` still opens it on all interfaces of the node running the task. Services that only talk to other services should use an overlay network instead of being published; otherwise the remaining control on the node is the `DOCKER-USER` chain.
- #2951: the Swarm ports (7946/tcp+udp and 4789/udp on every node, 2377/tcp on managers) should be allowed only from the other Swarm nodes; overlay traffic is unencrypted by default and VXLAN is unauthenticated ([GHSA-vwm3-crmr-xfxw](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-vwm3-crmr-xfxw)); `--opt encrypted` on untrusted links, with the caveats of CVE-2023-28840 and CVE-2023-28842.

As asked in #2951, there are no firewall rule sets or scripts, only links to the Docker documentation and the moby advisories.

2979.title: HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet: duplicate headers behind an Nginx reverse proxy
2979.body:
Adds one paragraph to the Nginx subsection of the HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet, right after the inheritance note, as agreed in #2977.

When Nginx proxies an application that already sends security headers, `add_header` adds its own copy and does not replace the upstream one, so the client can receive the same header twice with conflicting values. The paragraph explains this and shows how to drop the upstream copy with `proxy_hide_header` before adding your own.

Sources and checks:

- [`add_header`](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_headers_module.html#add_header): "Adds the specified field to a response header".
- [`proxy_hide_header`](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html#proxy_hide_header): "sets additional fields that will not be passed" from the proxied server's response.
- Reproduced on nginx 1.30.6 in a container, proxying an upstream that sends `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`. With only `add_header "X-Frame-Options" "DENY" always;` the response has two `X-Frame-Options` headers. With `proxy_hide_header X-Frame-Options;` added, it has one, `DENY`.
- On current master (5f2a48a): `markdownlint` and `textlint` pass on the changed file. `test:link-check` gives the same results with and without the change, and `test:workflow-approvals` passes.
